extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), third-party requesters, patent owners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_short: ex parte reexamination filing and procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and binding procedural requirements for preparing, filing, and processing requests and follow-on papers in ex parte reexamination (35 U.S.C. 302) before the USPTO, including evidence submission, service, correspondence, amendments, fees, and processing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of admissions as prior art evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner as to any matter affecting patentability may be utilized to determine the scope and content of the prior art in conjunction with patents and printed publications in a prior art rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The admission must stand on its own; information supplementing or further defining the admission would be improper. Admissions may reside in the patent file, be presented during reexamination, or be in litigation. A third party may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the record of the file or court record unless such admissions were entered into a court record; if entered into a court record and a copy filed, it could be admitted under MPEP § 2282 but would not be given weight as an admission for establishing an SNQ for reexamination or as a basis for rejecting claims. See Ex parte McGaughey, 6 USPQ2d 1334, 1337 (Bd. Pat. App. & Inter. 1988).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of prior art must be filed and legible
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of each patent or printed publication relied on or referred to in the request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 must be filed with the request (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the copy is not legible or its scanned image into IFW will not be legible, it is deemed not provided and a Notice of Failure to Comply will be issued (see MPEP § 2227). Color photographs and similar color submissions that are legible will be retained in an 'artifact' file. Non-English documents require an English translation of all necessary and pertinent parts (see MPEP § 609.04(a), III); an English summary or abstract is usually not sufficient. There is no assurance the Office will consider material beyond the submitted translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver for submission of U.S. patents and patent publications
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to submit copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon is waived with respect to U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications, unless specifically required by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This waiver follows 37 CFR 1.98, which excludes U.S. patents and U.S. patent publications from the requirement for submission of a legible copy of documents cited in an IDS, unless specifically required by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings/applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications (these can be mistaken for a new request/filing); instead provide the application/proceeding number and status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions of such copies that are not permitted entry may be returned, expunged, or discarded at the Office's discretion. Example: when the patent is a continuation-in-part, provide parent application number and status if relevant to the asserted SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the printed patent required
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesters must include a copy of the patent for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)(4)), to serve as the specification for the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full copy of the printed patent (double-column format preferred) including front page, abstract, drawings, specification, and claims. Include any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued, and copies of any federal court decision, complaint in a pending civil action, interference or derivation decision to present a complete history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service on patent owner (third-party requests)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the requester is a person other than the patent owner, the patent owner must be served with a copy of the request in its entirety and a certificate of service must be attached to the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must be made on the patent owner’s correspondence address as indicated in 37 CFR 1.33(c). The certificate must set forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service and be attached to the request; a copy of the certificate must also be included in the copy served on the patent owner. If service was not possible after reasonable effort, supply a duplicate copy to the Office with a cover letter explaining the efforts made. To avoid duplicate filing fees, requesters are strongly encouraged to clearly label the cover letter (example heading provided). See MPEP § 2266.03 regarding service on requester and patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments included in a patent owner’s request must comply with 37 CFR 1.530
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may include a proposed amendment with a request under 37 CFR 1.510(e), but any such amendment must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)–(j) and the formatting/requirements in MPEP § 2250.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amendment adds claims, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. While the request decision is based on the claims in effect at the time of the request (i.e., proposed amendments are disregarded when deciding whether to grant), if the request is granted subsequent prosecution will be on the basis of the claims as amended. Patent owners may also propose amendments in a statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b)/(c) or during prosecution per 37 CFR 1.550(b). See MPEP §§ 2234 and 2250.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on request uses claims in effect at filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should be decided on the wording of the patent claims in effect at that time (without any proposed amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision on whether to grant reexamination is made as though any proposed amendments had not been presented. If reexamination is granted, later prosecution is on the basis of claims as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence address for patent owner and signature requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner in a reexamination or supplemental examination proceeding are directed to the correspondence address in the patent file (37 CFR 1.33(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and papers filed on behalf of patent owners must be signed by the patent owner(s) or by an attorney/agent of record, or by a registered attorney or agent not of record acting under 37 CFR 1.34. To have a different attorney/agent receive correspondence, file a new power of attorney (see MPEP § 324). Sample PTO forms for power of attorney and change of correspondence address are provided (PTO/AIA/81B, PTO/SB/81C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing addresses and Mail Stop labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Mail Stop addresses are prescribed for submission of ex parte reexamination requests, inter partes reexamination requests, and patents in storage; papers should be labeled with the Mail Stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Mail Stop 'Ex Parte Reexam' Attn: Central Reexamination Unit, Commissioner for Patents, P.O. Box 1450, Alexandria, VA 22313-1450. Hand-carried/delivery service correspondence should be brought to the Customer Service Window, Randolph Building, 401 Dulany Street, Alexandria, VA 22314 and also marked 'Mail Stop Ex Parte Reexam.' It is strongly recommended the Mail Stop information be placed prominently on the first page in a sufficiently large font.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of attorney/agent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To withdraw from representation in a patent or reexamination proceeding, the practitioner must certify compliance with 37 CFR 11.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must state: (1) reasonable notice was given to the client prior to expiration of any response period that the practitioner intends to withdraw; (2) all papers and property (including funds) to which the client is entitled were delivered to the client or authorized representative; and (3) the client was notified of any responses that may be due and the relevant time frame. Reasonable notice allows time for the client to obtain new counsel. Practitioner responsibilities to inform a client or former client of correspondence that could significantly affect a matter before the Office continue despite withdrawal. See also MPEP § 402.06. A sample form for withdrawal is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted and prohibited modes of transmission for requests and follow-on papers
rubrics_metrics.description: An ex parte reexamination request may not be sent by facsimile transmission (FAX) (37 CFR 1.6(d)(5)), but subsequent ex parte reexamination correspondence may be faxed to the Central Reexamination Unit at (571) 273-9900.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective July 9, 2007, the USPTO accepts requests and follow-on papers via EFS-Web; the Legal Framework for EFS-Web describes permitted uses. All letters after filing should identify the proceeding by patent number, reexamination request control number, art unit, and examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificate of mailing and Priority Mail Express procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) may be used to file any paper in an ex parte reexamination proceeding except for a request for reexamination and a corrected/replacement request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes filing a patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 and a requester's reply under 37 CFR 1.535. The Priority Mail Express® (37 CFR 1.10) mailing procedure may also be used to file any paper in an ex parte reexamination proceeding (including patent owner statements and requester replies). See MPEP §§ 512 and 513.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely papers prior to order must not address merits
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request for ex parte reexamination (35 U.S.C. 302), no papers directed to the merits of the reexamination other than (A) citations of patents or printed publications under 37 CFR 1.501 or 1.555, (B) another complete request under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915, or (C) notifications pursuant to MPEP § 2282, should be filed prior to decision on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any other papers directed to merits filed prior to decision will be returned to sender by the CRU or Technology Center Director without consideration; if entered prior to discovery of the impropriety they will be expunged from the record. A copy of the letter providing notification of return/expungement will be made of record in the patent file; no copy of the returned/expunged papers will be retained. If appropriate later in proceedings, such submissions may be filed and accepted at that time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing and handling of incomplete reexamination requests
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP opens mail and performs initial clerical processing of reexamination requests; CRU checks reexamination filing date requirements and notifies requester of failure to comply using Form PTOL-2077.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request fails to meet filing-date requirements the requester is generally given one opportunity (usually 30 days) to complete the request. If the response introduces a new defect, the request will not be granted a filing date (absent extraordinary circumstances). Failure to timely or adequately respond may result in the request not being granted a filing date and placement of request papers in the patent file as a 37 CFR 1.501 citation. If a filing date was assigned and a non-compliance is discovered later, OPLA may issue a Decision Vacating Filing Date, normally giving the requester only one opportunity to correct non-compliance. Examples include payment issues (returned check) discovered after assignment of filing date but before decision on the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice of filed requests and Director-initiated orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of notice of filing of complete ex parte reexamination requests filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 will be made in the Official Gazette approximately 4–5 weeks after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both requests assigned a filing date and Director-initiated orders to reexamine made without a request will be announced. The notice appears under Requests for Ex Parte Reexamination Filed and will include the name of any requestor and other items required by 37 CFR 1.11(c). PALM/PALM staff prepare forms for printing in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice via Official Gazette if owner unreachable
rubrics_metrics.description: If all efforts to correspond with the patent owner fail because no current address is available, the reexamination proceeding will proceed without actual notice to the owner and publication in the Official Gazette will serve as constructive notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive notice applies to (A) notice of filing of a request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302 or (B) notice of ordering of reexamination at the Director's initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access to reexamination files
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination files are open to inspection by the general public via Public PAIR on the USPTO website, except for non-patent literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members of the public can view the entire content of the reexamination file except non-patent literature. Copies of reexamination files may be ordered from the Document Services Division of OPR (indicate control number), requested via email (dsd@uspto.gov) for a fee, or obtained from IFW via PAIR. Certified copies (CD-ROM) may be purchased from OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining if a reexamination request was filed via PAIR/PALM
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the USPTO Internet PAIR or intranet PALM to determine if a reexamination request has been filed for a given patent number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PALM: enter the patent number, click 'Search', then click 'Continuity Data' to obtain reexamination number. Note there is approximately a ten (10) day lag between filing and data entry into PALM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for reexamination and entity-based fee reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 carries fees for the request (37 CFR 1.20(c)(1)), for addition of claims (excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4)), for extensions of time, and for appeals, appeal forwarding fees, and oral hearing fees under 37 CFR 41.20(b). No fee is required for issuance of the reexamination certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions relating to reexamination require fees (37 CFR 1.17(m), 1.20(c)(6)). Micro entity reductions are available to patent owners only. Small entity and micro entity reductions are available to patent owners for excess claim fees, appeal, appeal forwarding, and oral hearing fees. For request and petition fees, small entity reductions are available to both third-party requesters and patent owners; micro entity reductions are available only to patent owners. In merged proceedings only a single fee is required even though multiple copies of submissions may be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for entry of amendments (37 CFR 1.530(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments in reexamination must follow § 1.530(d): specification changes, claims changes, drawings changes, and formal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification (other than claims): submit entire text of any added or rewritten paragraph including markings (or delete an entire paragraph by statement deleting it); identify the precise point where addition/rewrite is located. Claims: include entire text of each claim being changed and each new claim proposed; parenthetical like 'amended' or 'twice amended' should follow claim number; include markings pursuant to paragraph (f); a claim may be canceled by a statement canceling it without presenting its text. Drawings: submit a sketch on separate paper showing proposed changes in red for examiner approval; upon approval, file new sheets in compliance with § 1.84; amended figures identified as 'Amended', added figures as 'New', canceled figures bracketed and identified as 'Canceled.' Formal requirements for other papers are in § 1.52. Status/support: supply status (pending/canceled) of all claims as of the date of amendment on separate pages and an explanation of support in the disclosure for the claim changes. (Changes shown by markings per paragraph (f) — text continues beyond chunk.)
